tip: 약을 먹다 (yageul meokda) = take medicine: Korean normally uses the verb for eating, even for syrup.
다녀오다 (danyeooda) = go and come back: 다녀올게요 (danyeoolgeyo) = I'll be right back.
-지 말고 (-ji malgo) = don't do A, do B instead: 무리하지 말고 쉬세요 (murihaji malgo swiseyo).
Staff normally honor the customer: 오셨어요 (osyeosseoyo) is the respectful version of 왔어요 (wasseoyo) = did you come.
-아/어 볼게요 (-eo bolgeyo) = I'll just try doing it: 재 볼게요 (jae bolgeyo) = let me measure it.
-지 마세요 (-ji maseyo) = please don't: 걱정하지 마세요 (geokjeonghaji maseyo) = don't worry.
주사를 맞다 (jusareul matda) = get a shot: Korean normally uses the verb for being hit here, not 하다 (hada = do).
드릴게요 (deurilgeyo) = I'll give it, the humble form used when the favor is done for the listener.
치과 (chigwa) = dental clinic: -과 (-gwa) on a clinic name marks the medical specialty.
The pharmacist honors you: 있으세요 (isseuseyo) is the respectful version of 있어요 (isseoyo) = you have.
하루에 세 번 (harue se beon) = three times a day: 에 (e) here marks per.
후 (hu) = after and 전 (jeon) = before attach straight onto nouns: 식후에 (sikue) = after meals.
바르세요 (bareuseyo) is from 바르다 (bareuda) = spread on, the verb for creams, ointment and sunscreen.
소화제 (sohwaje) = digestion aid: -제 (-je) on the end normally names a type of medicine.
Korean splits tired: 졸려요 (jollyeoyo) = drowsy, ready to doze; 피곤해요 (pigonhaeyo) = worn out. Medicine makes you 졸려요 (jollyeoyo), the drowsy one.
Adjective + -아/어지다 (-ajida/-eojida) = become: 괜찮아질 거예요 (gwaenchanajil geoyeyo) = will get better.
보다 (boda) after a noun = than: 어제보다 (eojeboda) = than yesterday.
몸조리 잘하세요 (momjori jalhaseyo) is the set phrase for get well soon.
Elders normally don't get plain 아프다 (apeuda = sick): respect swaps in a different verb, 편찮으세요 (pyeonchaneuseyo) = grandmother is unwell.
An elder's pain still takes the respect ending: 아프세요 (apeuseyo), not 아파요 (apayo).
분 (bun) = the respectful word for counting people: 두 분 (du bun) = two people, politely.
만들어 드렸어요 (mandeureo deuryeosseoyo) uses 드리다 (deurida), the humble 'give' for elders – with a friend the same favor would end in 줬어요 (jwosseoyo).
유행 (yuhaeng) = going around: fashion and flu can both be 유행이에요 (yuhaengieyo).
-기 (-gi) makes a verb into a noun: 씻기 (ssitgi) = washing.
-에 좋아요 (-e joayo) = good for something: 건강에 좋아요 (geongange joayo) = good for your health.
배탈이 나다 (baetari nada) = get an upset stomach: the trouble breaks out rather than being caught.
-아/어 주세요 (-eo juseyo) = do it for me: 가 주세요 (ga juseyo) = please go with me.
-네요 (-neyo) = shared surprise: 좋네요 (jonneyo) = it's nice, isn't it.
안개가 끼다 (angaega kkida) = fog settles in: 안개가 꼈어요 (angaega kkyeosseoyo) = fog came in.
-기 쉬워요 (-gi swiwoyo) = easy to do: 걸리기 쉬워요 (geolligi swiwoyo) = easy to catch.
